A new report has ranked agriculture as the second-largest sector for technology-related activities in Kano State, behind only information and communications technology. The Kano Technology and Innovation Ecosystem Intelligence Report 2026 also revealed a significant gender gap in the state’s technology ecosystem, with women accounting for only 22 per cent of respondents, compared with 78 per cent for men. The Executive Director of Enovate Lab, Ahmed Idris, disclosed the findings on Thursday at the official launch of the report in Kano. Idris said the findings challenged the assumption that the state’s technology ecosystem was largely dominated by ICT companies and start-ups. “Before conducting this research, I personally assumed that the ecosystem was predominantly focused on ICT. He said the findings reflected Kano’s economic strengths in agricultural production, commodity markets and commerce, which could create opportunities for technology-driven businesses. Idris urged entrepreneurs and investors to explore agricultural technology, healthcare technology and other emerging areas rather than concentrating mainly on software development. “We must begin thinking globally while developing solutions locally,” he said. On the challenges facing the ecosystem, Idris identified inadequate funding, limited awareness of available opportunities and knowledge gaps as major constraints for organisations and entrepreneurs. Speaking earlier, the Programme Manager and representative of eHealth Africa, Fatimah Huweidy, said the organisation supported the initiative because of its longstanding commitment to Kano. “Kano is central to our story. This is our headquarters. eHealth Africa has one headquarters, and it is located here in Kano. This demonstrates our commitment to the people and the region,” she said. Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, represented by his Special Adviser on Information and Technology, Yusuf Sharada, described the report as timely. “I want to appreciate those who came up with this idea, particularly Enovate Lab, for bringing stakeholders together to ensure that we have a report that the government and other stakeholders can use as a benchmark to assess where we are and where we are heading,” he said. The governor said his administration would examine the report’s recommendations and consider how they could be implemented to support the state’s development priorities. The report was supported by Enovate Lab, the Kano State Information Technology Development Agency, eHealth Africa and other organisations. Hussaini Ibrahim
